info.bio:
Testament es una de las bandas más grandes de thrash metal. De hecho, el quinteto de San Francisco en algún momento pareció desafiar a Metallica (su influencia más obvia en un principio) en las apuestas del power thrash metal. 

Sin embargo, su carrera a la cima fracasó principalmente debido a la inconsistencia, las malas decisiones de negocios, y la cada vez menor popularidad del género a comienzos de los 90 en favor de otros estilos musicales como el emergente grunge.

scenes.name: Speed/thrash metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Si el lite metal es la corriente latitudinaria, el speed/thrash es la fundamentalista: un retorno a los principios de la subcultura heavy que, como todo fundamentalismo, es tanto un comienzo nuevo como una continuación. Nace en California en 1981-83 con Metallica en Los Ángeles y Exodus en San Francisco; hacia 1982 hay una escena de fans que intercambian maquetas y grabaciones piratas, y durante años solo graba en sellos independientes y suena en programas de radio universitaria: «underground» también en lo comercial. Bebe de la NWOBHM (Venom, Diamond Head, Iron Maiden) y del punk y el hardcore. Weinstein lo compara con la Reforma protestante: fuera la ropa de escena, el atrezo y la distancia; los músicos visten vaqueros y camiseta, se mezclan con el público y se tiran a él desde el escenario. Acelera el tempo, renuncia a lo dionisíaco (el alcohol y las drogas son malos, no hay sexo) y se especializa en un caos concreto: alienación, corrupción política, destrucción ambiental, una retórica de canción protesta.

scenes.name: Speed y thrash metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La escena «street» de Los Ángeles cruza el hardcore (Bad Brains, Black Flag) con el glam-metal. A partir de una intuición de D.R.I., Metallica inventan el speed-metal: del thrash de Kill 'Em All a la elegancia casi clásica de Master Of Puppets. Megadeth, Slayer (puente entre el black metal de Venom y el death metal), Exciter, la escena de San Francisco (Death Angel, Exodus, Testament), Anthrax y White Zombie en Nueva York, y Sepultura, que lo convierten en lenguaje universal (Roots).

xref.title: Live Collaboration on "Wake Up" (2005)
xref.body: David Bowie recorded a live version of Arcade Fire's song "Wake Up Together" with the band at the Fashion Rocks event in New York in September 2005, a testament to his admiration and their mutual respect. "Here's the version of Wake Up featuring David Bowie. This was recorded at the Fashion Rocks event in New York in September of 2005."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Who the Hell is Arcade Fire? Part 1

xref.title: Acknowledging Heritage Live
xref.body: Chuck Billy frequently acknowledges his Native American heritage when Testament performs live, bringing awareness to his background. "He often acknowledges that when the band plays live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Indigenous Alternative

xref.title: Connections to Other Metal Bands
xref.body: In addition to his work with Testament, Chuck Billy has contributed to another metal band, Exodus, and was once considered for the role of frontman for Sepultura. He is also friends with many other prominent figures in the metal scene. "In addition to working with Testament, he's also contributed to Exodus, another metal band. And once had a shot at being the frontman for Sepulchura. He's also friends with a ton of other big name metal dudes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Indigenous Alternative

xref.title: Considered the "GOAT" of Guitar Techs
xref.body: Within the music business, Dallas Schoo is regarded by many as the "GOAT" (Greatest Of All Time) among guitar technicians, a testament to his skill and experience. "There are those in the business who consider him to be the goat of guitar techs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Continued Reverence
xref.body: As pioneers of the early 2000s indie rock revival centered in New York, The Strokes maintain a revered status among fans and critics, testament to their lasting influence on guitar-based rock music. "The strokes continued to be revered."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 9: (20-11)

xref.title: Dreadlocks as Rastafarian Symbol of Lion of Judah
xref.body: As a devoted Rastafarian, Bob Marley wore dreadlocks as a powerful religious symbol representing the Lion of Judah, a sacred emblem deeply rooted in Old Testament traditions. "He was a Rastafarian and dreads were a symbol of the lion of Judah, a religious symbol that stretches all the way back into the Old Testament."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: New Rock Hair

xref.title: Juno Award for Songwriters of the Year - Funeral
xref.body: Arcade Fire won a Juno Award for Songwriters of the Year, a testament to the strength and originality of their material on the *Funeral* album. "And they won a Juno for Songwriters of the Year."

xref.title: Long-Term Relevance and Longevity
xref.body: Elvis Costello is celebrated as one of the rare survivors from the 1970s punk scene who remains relevant, continues to make records, receives major mainstream media coverage, is revered by top songwriters, and can still headline large venues like the Molson Amphitheatre in Toronto. His career is considered a testament to artistic growth and perseverance. "How many survivors from the 1970s punk scene are A, not only making records, but B, still considered relevant, C, still accorded major coverage in the mainstream media, D, admired, if not revered by some of the best songwriters in the world, and E, still be able to be booked into large theaters like the Moulson Amphitheater in Toronto."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Elvis Costello

xref.title: Major Label Deal
xref.body: By the close of the 2010s, 100 gecs had secured a major label recording deal, a testament to their growing popularity and the perceived potential of their Hyperpop sound. "and by the end of the decade, 100 gecks had themselves a major label recording deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

xref.title: Massive Sales on Epitaph
xref.body: The Offspring achieved immense commercial success while signed to the independent label Epitaph. They were the "orange band" that eventually sold 20 million records on their own, a testament to Epitaph's ability to support and distribute successful artists without being a major label. "Until they signed this orange band called the offspring who eventually sold 20 million records on their own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt-Rock: Chapter 8

xref.title: Musical Proficiency and Collaboration with Barbra Streisand
xref.body: The members of Fanny were highly skilled musicians, capable of working as studio musicians. In 1971, their talent was recognized when none other than Barbra Streisand hired them to appear on one of her albums, a testament to their professional caliber. "In 1971, no one less than Barbara Streisand hired them to appear on one of her albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

xref.title: Ongoing Touring Presence
xref.body: The Cure continues to tour today, maintaining their legacy and connection with fans, a testament to their enduring influence in rock music. "The Cure continues to tour today, and if you're looking for bands influenced by them we can turn to groups like Interpol, Smashing Pumpkins, The Killers, Nine-H Nails, My Chemical Romance, and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 7: The Other Genres

xref.title: Parallel Ascent with Indie Music
xref.body: R.E.M.'s evolution from a "fratboy band" to intelligent, articulate, and politically aware superstars mirrored the rise of indie music in America. For many, R.E.M. served as an entry point into a rock and roll universe that had remained largely undetected by the mainstream for over a decade, and their popularity growth was a testament to the power of college radio. "REM's rise from fratboy band to intelligent, articulate, and politically aware superstars paralleled the ascent of indie music in America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

xref.title: Polaris Music Prize Winner
xref.body: In 2015, at the age of 74, Buffy Sainte-Marie won the Polaris Music Prize for her album "Power in the Blood," a testament to her enduring artistic relevance and impact. "In 2015, at the age of 74, she won the Polaris Music Prize for her album Power in the Blood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Indigenous Alternative

xref.title: Pomo Heritage
xref.body: Chuck Billy, whose real name is Charles Billy, is the frontman of Testament. His father was Native American, specifically from the Pomo tribe, which is indigenous to Northern California. "Their frontman is a guy named Chuck Billy and that's his real name, Charles Billy. ... his father was Native American. He's of the Pomo, a tribe indigenous to Northern California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Indigenous Alternative

xref.title: Reunion Performances
xref.body: Following their rediscovery, the band was enticed to reunite and even performed at one of Joey Ramone's Memorial birthday parties, a testament to their newly recognized status in punk history. "The band was enticed to reunite and even performed at one of Joey Ramones Memorial birthday parties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

xref.title: Running Crazed Management
xref.body: In addition to her label work, Marsha Zazula also operated Crazed Management. Her management roster included notable artists such as Ace Frehley of Kiss, Ministry, Testament, and King's X, demonstrating her significant role in artist development and career guidance. "She also ran crazed management, which included clients like Ace Freely of Kiss, Ministry, Testament, and King's X."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Unsung Heroines

xref.title: Time Magazine Cover - Funeral Success
xref.body: The overwhelming success of their *Funeral* album led to Arcade Fire being featured on the cover of Time Magazine, a testament to their rapid rise to prominence and critical recognition. "They ended up on the cover of Time Magazine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Who the Hell is Arcade Fire? Part 1

xref.title: Top-Grossing Tours
xref.body: Metallica is included in the group of artists, whose average age is 45 and above, that dominate the list of all-time top-grossing tours. Their ongoing ability to fill arenas is a testament to the powerful influence of nostalgia and the enduring loyalty of fans.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)

xref.title: Zero Lineup Changes
xref.body: Since their formation in 1991, Sloan has remarkably maintained the same four members, a testament to their enduring chemistry and "uber democratic structure." This stability is a significant factor in their ability to survive the music business for decades. "Many band who has survived this long in this country with zero lineup changes has got to have some stories."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 2
